From: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@pioneerhealthtech.com>

Cc: procurement@pioneerhealthtech.com
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request for remediation allowance and credit for 2027-07-26 incident

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the incident summary you posted earlier. Pioneer HealthTech observed a service interruption on 2027-07-26 in us-west-2 that affected our live inference endpoints (model: ph-encoder-v2). The window we measured from our side: 2027-07-26 02:10 UTC -> 2027-07-26 07:45 UTC (approx 335 minutes of failures, repeated 503s and queue timeouts). That resulted in several production jobs being retried and a visible outage for some downstream services.

Per our contract (SLA section), we believe this exceeds the monthly availability guarantee. Please advise on:
- Whether Pioneer HealthTech is eligible for a remediation credit for July 2027;
- The calculation method you will use (minutes, percentage of month, or SLO-deficit approach);
- Expected timeline to issue any approved credit and whether it will be a credit note or invoice adjustment.

I've attached a small packet from our monitoring team with timestamps and sample request ids. Happy to provide anything else you need.

Thanks,
Tom
Head of Platform
Pioneer HealthTech

I'll aim to get back with a preliminary number within 48 business hours after we reconcile logs.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Pioneer HealthTech outage — credit calculation and recommendation

Lauren / Marissa — internal calculation after reconciling telemetry:

Summary of reconciliation:
- Customer-reported window: 2027-07-26 02:10 -> 2027-07-26 07:45 UTC = 335 minutes total.
- Redwood-inferred affected window (requests returning 503 / connection failures): 2027-07-26 02:12 -> 2027-07-26 07:40 UTC = 328 minutes.
- Monthly minutes for July 2027 = 31 days * 24 * 60 = 44,640 minutes.
- Allowed downtime under 99.9% SLO = 0.1% of month = 44.64 minutes.
- Effective breach minutes = max(0, 328 - 44.64) = 283.36 minutes.

Calculation method (per contract section 4.2 and typical Redwood practice):
- Breach percentage = breach_minutes / total_month_minutes = 283.36 / 44,640 = 0.006345 (~0.6345%).
- Customer's committed monthly spend (from their July invoice): $45,000 (see attached).
- Remediation credit = breach_percentage * monthly_commitment = 0.006345 * $45,000 = $285.53.
- Round to nearest dollar for credit note => $286.

Recommendation & approvals:
- Amount is below Redwood's $10k operational approval threshold; Finance can issue directly as a credit note applied to the next invoice.
- For transparency, include supporting calc sheet and the reconciled telemetry log.

Attachments: calc_sheet_pioneer_20270802.xlsx (internal), incident_reconciled_log_20270726.csv

Karthik
Sr. Engineering Manager, Runtime Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Remediation credit approved and issuance details for Pioneer HealthTech (Jul 2027)

Hi Tom — following up with the confirmed calculation and next steps. Apologies again for the impact; we've completed the reconciliation with engineering.

What we found:
- Confirmed outage window attributable to Redwood: 2027-07-26 02:12 -> 2027-07-26 07:40 UTC (328 minutes).
- Effective breach after SLO allowance: 283.36 minutes.
- Calculated remediation credit (rounded): $286. This is based on the breach percentage of the month applied against the committed monthly spend ($45,000).

Issuance plan:
- Finance will issue a credit note for $286 and apply it against Pioneer HealthTech's next invoice (no action required from you).
- Credit note reference: CN-2027-4892-08 (attached).
- Expected posting date: within 5 business days.

I've attached: credit_note_20270803.pdf (formal note) and the reconciled incident log. If you'd prefer the credit show as an invoice adjustment rather than a credit note, let me know and we'll route that to accounts receivable.

Separately, engineering shared the root cause writeup (link below) and the mitigation steps we've applied to prevent recurrence (rate-limiter fix and improved cross-AZ failover for prefix cache). If you'd like a short review call with Karthik and your platform team we can schedule it.

Helpful links: https://redwood.company/pm/incident/2027-07-26-usa-west-2

Thanks for your patience — we value Pioneer as a customer and will follow through to make sure the remediation is clear on your billing.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
